p: Chaired by Arvind Panagariya (members T. Rabi Sankar, Annie George Mathew, Manoj Panda, Soumya Kanti Ghosh); award period 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031; report tabled 1 February 2026. Articles 270(1) (tax sharing), 275(1) (grants-in-aid) and 282 (discretionary grants).

Devolution share is unchanged from the 15th Commission (which cut the 14th's 42%); the divisible pool excludes cesses, surcharges, UT taxes and collection costs. Criteria changes: demographic performance uses 1971-2011 population growth, forest includes open forest, 'tax effort' replaced by contribution to GDP (square root of GSDP).

Local bodies: grants-in-aid Rs 9.47 lakh crore (Rs 4.4 lakh crore rural, Rs 3.6 lakh crore urban; urban share up from 36% to 45%); 80% basic and 20% performance grants; half of basic grants tied to sanitation, waste and water; revenue-deficit and sector-specific grants dropped.

Disasters: State Disaster Relief and Management Funds corpus Rs 2,04,401 crore; 90:10 for NE and Himalayan States, 75:25 others; heatwave and lightning to be notified as national disasters. Fiscal: Centre's deficit 3.5% of GDP by 2030-31; States 3% of GSDP; review of 308 inactive State PSEs; stop off-budget borrowing; DISCOM SPVs and privatisation.

Census urban definition: settlement over 5,000, at least 75% of male workers non-agricultural, density at least 400 per sq km (plus statutory towns). Kerala is 47.7% urban by Census 2011, but functional urbanisation is much higher.

Budget steps: City Economic Regions (Rs 5,000 crore each over five years), Rs 100 crore incentive for a municipal bond over Rs 1,000 crore, five university townships, Urban Challenge Fund Rs 1 lakh crore.
Problems: cities raise under 0.6% of GDP in own revenue (OECD 2-4%); low Floor Space Index raises land costs; waste collection 98% of wards but processing lags; no strong mayor.

73rd and 74th Amendments added Part IX (Panchayats) and IXA (Municipalities); three tiers mandatory above 20 lakh population; fresh election within six months of dissolution; one-third seats for women; PESA 1996 extends Part IX to Fifth Schedule areas.

History: Balwant Rai Mehta (1957, three tiers), first PRI at Nagaur on 2 October 1959, Ashok Mehta (two tiers). Tools: Devolution Index, eGramSwaraj linked to GeM, SVAMITVA drone mapping, Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (CSS from 2022-23).

Numbers: women about 40% of PRI leaders; fiscal decentralisation from Rs 2.36 lakh crore (15th FC) to Rs 4.35 lakh crore (16th FC); panchayats' own revenue only 1.1% of their income. VB-G RAM G law gives 125 days of guaranteed rural work (up from 100).

Supreme Court worried that unconditional cash transfers may reduce work incentives; S. Subramaniam Balaji (2013) upheld colour TVs and laptops as consistent with DPSPs; Section 123 RPA 1951 bars bribing electors. Economic Survey: unconditional transfers (esp. to women) about Rs 1.7 lakh crore in 2025-26; the number of States with them is projected to rise more than fivefold between 2022-23 and 2025-26.

PM RAHAT (MoRTH): cashless treatment up to Rs 1.5 lakh for 7 days after any road accident, stabilisation up to 24 or 48 hours, claims paid in 10 days by the State Health Agency from the Motor Vehicle Accident Fund; State Road Safety Council is nodal; linked with 112.

Corruption Perception Index (Transparency International): India 91st (from 96th) with score 39; Denmark first (89) for the eighth time; CPI covers public-sector perceived corruption only (not private sector, money laundering or citizens' experience).

Environmental laws: public trust doctrine (M.C. Mehta v Kamal Nath 1996); concerns - land acquisition before EIA for non-coal mining (since 18 December 2025), 100 m height rule for Aravalli, recall of Vanashakti (2025).

Gender Budget: adopted 2004-05, now 9.37% of the Union Budget (Part A 100% women's schemes, Part B at least 30%). Motion of Thanks (Article 87(1): President's address); opposition moved removal of Lok Sabha Speaker; NOTA (PUCL 2013, first in 2013 State polls; winner is next highest); Right to Recall idea; Article 3 (Parliament can create or alter States by simple majority with President's prior recommendation).
Frontier Nagaland Territorial Authority: covers Tuensang, Mon, Kiphire, Longleng, Noklak, Shamator; 46 subjects devolved; agreement among the Centre, Nagaland and ENPO; Article 371(A) unaffected.

WTO: Appellate Body non-functional because the US blocks appointments; Doha Round (2001) unfinished; consensus rule lets one member block; EU's CBAM seen as a trade barrier; regional blocs (RCEP) challenge multilateralism; near-shoring vs friend-shoring.

India-France: now a Special Global Strategic Partnership, with an annual Foreign Ministers' Comprehensive Dialogue for Horizon 2047 and the 2026 Year of Innovation; H125 final assembly line (Tata-Airbus), MRO for LEAP and M-88 engines, BEL-Safran HAMMER munitions; France is second largest defence supplier; co-presidents of ISA and CDRI; trade 12.67 billion euros (2024-25).

India-US trade deal: reciprocal tariff cut from 25% to 18%, the extra 25% Russian-oil duty withdrawn (Aug 2025 had a 50% total); trade 132.2 billion dollars in FY25; US FDI 70.65 billion dollars (2000-2025).

India-GCC FTA terms of reference finalised (GCC 1981, Riyadh; six members; India-GCC trade 178.56 billion dollars in 2024-25; GCC GDP 2.3 trillion dollars). Israel: Special Strategic Partnership, up to 50,000 workers over five years. Malaysia: Comprehensive Strategic Partnership (Aug 2024), Harimau Shakti 5th edition.

Seychelles: full member of the Colombo Security Conclave (India, Sri Lanka, Mauritius, Maldives, Bangladesh), joins CDRI, India gives 175 million dollars. Brazil: trade goal raised from 20 to 30 billion dollars by 2030; trade 15.21 billion in 2025; co-founder of Global Biofuel Alliance; strategic partner since 2006.
Power Gap Index (Lowy; 27 countries, 131 indicators): India -4.0 in 2025, below potential.
IONS (2008, India's initiative; 25 members): India took the chair. Combined Maritime Forces: India led Combined Task Force-154 for the first time.

FORGE succeeds the Minerals Security Partnership (critical minerals ministerial in Washington, 50+ countries incl. India); Project Vault is a US public-private critical mineral stockpile. New START (signed 2010, in force 2011) capped deployed warheads at 1,550 each and has expired, the last binding US-Russia limit.

NATO's Arctic Sentry (Joint Force Command Norfolk) guards the Arctic. Places: Rafah (Gaza-Egypt), Donetsk and Luhansk (Donbas), Diego Garcia (Chagos; UK 2025 deal to return Chagos to Mauritius with a 99-year lease), El-Fasher and Darfur (Sudan).

Reforms: Business Reforms Action Plan (2014, DPIIT); Regulatory Compliance Burden initiative (2020, about 47,000 compliances cut); Jan Vishwas Act 2023 (183 provisions in 42 Acts); SPICe+ (10 services); ULIP (35+ systems); MCA21 v3; National Single Window; PM GatiShakti; India ranked 63 in the 2019 Doing Business Report (up 79 places).
Gaps: over 4.6 crore pending cases, Rs 25 lakh crore stuck in commercial disputes, dispute resolution about 1,400 days against 400 globally, unclear land titles; D-BRAP at district level.

Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (MeitY) raised from Rs 22,919 crore to Rs 40,000 crore; ISM 2.0 targets fabrication, packaging and equipment; rare earth corridors in Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu; three chemical parks; a construction and infrastructure equipment scheme; revival of 200 legacy clusters; Mega Textile Parks (challenge mode).

Finance: Rs 10,000 crore SME Growth Fund and Rs 2,000 crore top-up to the Self-Reliant India Fund (2021); 5-year tax holiday for non-residents supplying capital goods; deferred duty for trusted manufacturers; one digital customs window.

Components context: India imports core components (China, South Korea, Vietnam); production costs 10-20% above China, Vietnam, Mexico; scheme offers 6-year turnover-linked, 5-year capex and hybrid incentives; SPECS gives 25% capex support; National Policy on Electronics 2019; global e-waste to reach 82 million tonnes by 2030.

Rs 10,000 crore over five years: 3 new NIPERs and 7 upgraded, over 1,000 accredited clinical trial sites, a scientific review cadre at CDSCO. SHAKTI = Strategy for Healthcare Advancement through Knowledge, Technology and Innovation.
Bioeconomy grew from 10 billion dollars (2014) to 165.7 billion (2024), 4.25% of GDP; shares: BioIndustrial 47%, BioPharma 35%, Bioresearch 9%, BioAgri 8%; target 300 billion dollars by 2030.

Biologics are medicines from living sources (vaccines, blood components); biosimilars are highly similar copies. National Biopharma Mission runs under BIRAC (DBT); three bulk drug parks (Gujarat, Himachal, Andhra Pradesh; Rs 3,000 crore); FDI 100% automatic for greenfield pharma, 74% for brownfield; 'evergreening' is tweaking drugs near patent expiry.

Budget: all CPSE purchases from MSMEs via TReDS; GeM linked to TReDS; TReDS receivables as asset-backed securities; CGTMSE guarantee for invoice discounting; Corporate Mitras. TReDS (RBI, 2018): only MSMEs sell; buyers are corporates, departments and PSUs.

Classification by investment and turnover; limits raised 2.5x and 2x from 1 April 2025. MSMEs: over 7.47 crore units, 32.82 crore jobs, 31.1% of GDP, 35.4% of manufacturing, 48.58% of exports, 51% in rural areas; only about 1.1% of Udyam units export.
Problems: finance is the top barrier (21.5%); 97.92% are micro and 0.01% medium (the 'missing middle'); only 5.8% innovate against 24.9% in South Asia.
Support: Udyam Registration (2020), Udyam Assist (2023), 25% procurement from micro and small units, RAMP (World Bank), PM Vishwakarma (18 trades).

topics.t: Startup recognition framework and orange economy
p: Startups: turnover limit raised from Rs 100 crore to Rs 200 crore; age limit 10 years; multi-State and State cooperative societies now eligible; deep tech startups get 20 years and Rs 300 crore; DPIIT recognises; split-up or reconstructed entities are ineligible.

Orange economy (Ivan Duque Marquez and Felipe Buitrago, 2013): creativity-based industries (AVGC, film, music, design, crafts). Budget: AVGC labs in 15,000 secondary schools and 500 colleges via IICT Mumbai, a new National Institute of Design in the east (seven exist). Creative exports rose 20% to over 11 billion dollars (2023-24); over 10 million livelihoods; UNGA declared 2021 International Year of Creative Economy; India Cine Hub; Cinematograph Amendment Act 2023 (anti-piracy); WAVES platform.

Economic Survey borrows 'entrepreneurial state' from Mariana Mazzucato: barriers are retrospective scrutiny of good-faith decisions, fear of trying new things, subsidies hardening into commitments and RTI chilling candid talk; Japan's 'fair accountability' and South Korea's safe spaces are cited.

National Monetisation Pipeline 2.0 (NITI Aayog): Rs 16.72 lakh crore over FY26-FY30 across 12 sectors; NMP 1.0 (2021, 13 sectors, Rs 6 lakh crore) reached 89%; idea from Vijay Kelkar Committee (2012); focuses on brownfield assets; models include TOT, OMT, ROMT, REITs and InvITs.

topics.t: Female labour force participation and Lakhpati Didi
p: Survey: raising FLFPR to about 55% by 2050 is critical; India fell from 129th to 131st in the WEF Gender Gap Report 2025; U-curve explains the dip in early industrialisation; women are 43% of STEM graduates but about 27% of the STEM workforce; they spend 363 minutes a day on unpaid work against 123 for men; 28% of platform workers; 31% cite commuting as a barrier (World Bank 2021).
Laws: 26 weeks paid maternity leave and 12 weeks for adoptive and commissioning mothers; creches below six; night work allowed in factories in about 22 States/UTs and commercial units in 33.

Lakhpati Didi (2023, DAY-NRLM, Rural Development): 3 crore target achieved early; new goal 6 crore by March 2029; household income above Rs 1 lakh a year (about Rs 10,000 a month); Revolving Fund Rs 20,000-30,000 per SHG, Community Investment Fund up to Rs 2.5 lakh; BC Sakhis; Project eShakti (NABARD); SHE-Mart in Budget 2026-27.

Capital goods: about 12% of manufacturing output, 40% imported; market 92 billion dollars vs production 32 billion; R&D 0.9% of GDP vs 2.8% target; National Capital Goods Policy 2016 aimed to raise share from 12% to 20% by 2025; draft 2025 policy; Budget 2026-27 raises capex 9% to Rs 12.2 lakh crore; two CPSE tool rooms; duty exemption for lithium-ion cell machinery; Rs 10,000 crore for container manufacturing; a CIE scheme; India joined the Washington Accord (engineering) as a permanent member.

Textiles: 2% of GDP, 11% of manufacturing GVA, 6th largest exporter, US and EU about 47% of exports, 80% of capacity with MSMEs, over 90% of weaving unorganised. Budget: National Fibre Scheme, Textile Expansion and Employment Scheme, Mahatma Gandhi Gram Swaraj initiative, Handloom and Handicraft Programme, Tex-Eco, Samarth 2.0; US tariff of 50% is a challenge; India-EU FTA to give zero duty; Kapas Kisan app and Kasturi Cotton Bharat.

topics.t: Grain storage and economy news in brief (February)
p: Record foodgrain output 353.96 million tonnes (2024-25); Central Pool storage 917.83 lakh tonnes (1 July 2025); 60-70% of grain is stored at household level; Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (2020) and Agricultural Marketing Infrastructure help build PACS-level storage.

Debt-to-GDP 55.6% (BE 2026-27), heading to 50 plus or minus 1% by 2030-31 and now the main fiscal anchor over the deficit. APA safe harbour threshold raised from Rs 300 crore to Rs 2,000 crore; IT services merged into one category; APAs finish in 2 years (+6 months). LRS (2004): resident individuals including minors can send USD 2.5 lakh a year; not for corporates, firms, HUFs or trusts.

PACS: Multi-State PACS (Entry 44, Union List) and single-State (Entry 32, State List); Multi-State Cooperative Societies (Amendment) Act 2023 requires women and SC/ST board members; model bye-laws let PACS run as multipurpose centres. Integrated farming (89.4% of farmers have under 2 hectares). RRTS: up to 180 km/h, run by NCRTC.
Rare earth magnets: 60-80% imported from China (2022-25); REPM scheme Rs 7,280 crore, 6,000 MTPA. Three chemical parks (Rs 600 crore); chemicals about 7% of GDP, R&D 0.7% vs 2.3% global.

topics.t: Prahaar counter-terrorism policy and border technology
p: Prahaar is India's first national counter-terrorism policy (MHA), with seven pillars; NSG is the nodal counter-terror force; Multi Agency Centre and the IB's Joint Task Force on Intelligence share information; laws include UAPA 1967 and PMLA 2002; MLATs and extradition for foreign cooperation; local police are first responders.

Border technology: CIBMS Stages II and III to cover about 1,955 km; BOLD-QIT was a pilot; a Border Security Technology Oversight Authority is proposed; challenges are drones, tunnels, unfenced terrain and cyber attacks.
Exercise Khanjar (India-Kyrgyzstan), MILAN (biennial multilateral naval, hosted by India), Vayu Shakti (IAF firepower), Dharma Guardian (with Japan).

Vibrant Villages: VVP-I (2023, Centrally Sponsored, northern border) and VVP-II (2025, Central Sector, land borders of 15 States and 2 UTs). INS Anjadip (third of 8 ASW shallow-water craft, GRSE, Hull Mounted Sonar Abhay, 'Dolphin Hunter').
Budget 2026-27: Rs 20,000 crore over five years; NITI Aayog target 750 million tonnes a year of CO2 capture and storage; it is the only route for steel, cement, petrochemicals and fertiliser.

Storage: enhanced oil recovery, enhanced coal bed methane, saline aquifers and basalt; risks include rock fracture and micro-earthquakes; direct air capture costs 400-800 dollars per tonne; hubs possible in the Krishna-Godavari basin and Rajasthan.
Supreme Court gave NGT primary monitoring of river pollution (suo motu 2021) and reaffirmed a clean environment under Article 21; M.C. Mehta (1987) restrained Ganga polluters.

CPCB: 296 polluted stretches on 271 rivers; only 62% of 2,116 locations meet BOD under 3 mg/L; CWC: metals above limit at 112 of 434 stations; only 69% of Namami Gange funds used by 2024-25; over 60% of sewage reaches rivers untreated.
Laws: Water Act 1974 (CPCB, SPCBs), Environment Protection Act 1986, NGT Act 2010; EU Water Framework Directive cited as a model.

Paris Agreement Article 6: 6.2 (bilateral accounting), 6.4 (crediting mechanism; first credits approved), 6.8 (non-market cooperation). Great Nicobar project: NGT upheld clearance; transshipment port, airport, 450 MVA power plant, about 130 sq km forest diverted; Shompen concerns; about 75% of India's transshipment is handled abroad.

IOC (UNESCO, Paris; India among 152 members) released the Integrated Ocean Carbon report (solubility pump). Rat-hole mining (NGT banned 2014). Fishing cat: Vulnerable, Schedule I, West Bengal's State animal. NHAI bee corridors; only female bees sting. Peatlands: drainage and fires cause at least 5% of global emissions; Congo Basin peat holds about a third of tropical peat carbon.

topics.t: Dowry in India and migration survey
p: Dowry Prohibition Act 1961 covers gifts before, at or after marriage; Satvir Singh (2001): anything demanded in connection with marriage is dowry; Rajbir (2010): add murder charge in dowry deaths; Ajmal Beg (2025): appoint trained Dowry Prohibition Officers; Arnesh Kumar: no automatic arrest in 498-A cases.

Dowry crimes rose 14% in 2023 (over 15,000 cases, 6,100 deaths; Uttar Pradesh most). A migration survey runs July 2026 to June 2027; overall migration rate was 28.9% (PLFS 2020-21): 47.9% women, 10.7% men.

First global AI summit in the Global South (earlier: Bletchley 2023, Seoul 2024, Paris 2025 co-chaired by India and France); structured as 7 Chakras and 3 Sutras; theme 'People, Planet, Progress'; New Delhi Declaration endorsed by 92 countries and organisations; three sovereign AI models launched (Sarvam, Gnani.ai, BharatGen Param2).

MANAV vision: Moral and Ethical, Accountable governance, National sovereignty, Accessible and inclusive, Valid and legitimate; IT Rules amendment 2026 on synthetic media; phases: small open-weight models, an AI Safety Institute, then compute autonomy.

AI in health and farming: MadhuNetrAI, eSanjeevani decision support, SAHI strategy, TB risk prediction (27% fewer adverse outcomes), Ayurgenomics, a cancer image biobank; Bharat-VISTAAR, Kisan e-Mitra, AgriStack, YES-TECH, CROPIC, WINDS.

NQM: 8-year mission (Science and Technology Ministry), hubs: IISc Bengaluru (computing), IIT Madras (communication), IIT Bombay (sensing and metrology), IIT Delhi (materials and devices); target 133-qubit computer by 2026; 'Triple Helix' of government, industry and academia; QpiAI-Indus 25-qubit; QuEST 2018; quantum is dual-use (Wassenaar).
Qubits are fragile and lose coherence from noise; need near absolute-zero temperatures; India's GERD about 0.7%.

LIGO-India (Aundh, Hingoli, Maharashtra; built by L&T under DAE; DAE and DST with US NSF): L-shaped interferometer with two 4 km arms; LIGO's US sites Hanford and Livingston; Einstein predicted gravitational waves in 1916; GW170817 (neutron star merger, 2017); Nobel 2017 to Weiss, Barish and Thorne; network includes Virgo, KAGRA, GEO600.

DRDO tested Solid Fuel Ducted Ramjet at Chandipur. Mons Mouton (near the Moon's south pole) is the landing site for a 2027 sample-return mission. NLST (2 m, Merak, Ladakh) and NLOT (13.7 m, Hanle). Davos Compact on AMR; nafithromycin (2024) is India's first indigenous antibiotic for resistant bacteria; National Action Plan on AMR 2.0 (2025-29).
Kerala declared Bacillus subtilis its State microbe. Organ transplants rose almost fourfold (under 5,000 in 2013 to about 20,000 in 2025); THOTA 1994 (NOTTO, ROTTO, SOTTO).
Bharat GI: DPIIT's umbrella initiative to show India's GI products, launched at the AI Impact Summit.

Tamil Brahmi inscriptions from the 1st-3rd centuries CE mention traders (Cikai Korran). Ol Chiki script (Raghunath Murmu, 1925) for Santhali (Austroasiatic; Eighth Schedule by the 92nd Amendment 2003); centenary inaugurated by the President.

topics.t: Ethics of war and AI autonomy
p: Just war theory (Augustine, Aquinas): jus ad bellum (when), jus in bello (how, proportionality), jus post bellum. Law: Geneva Conventions 1949, Genocide Convention 1948, ICC (Rome Statute 1998), Hague Conventions 1899 and 1907, MTCR, CTBT, BWC and CWC, NPT and TPNW.

Moltbook (Jan 2026; AI bots only; over 2 million bots) raises issues: black box, alignment, closed-loop misinformation, accountability. Frameworks: UNESCO AI ethics recommendation 2021, OECD AI Principles 2019, EU AI Act 2024, Bletchley Declaration; the text recommends a national AI authority and human-in-the-loop oversight.

topics.t: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana
p: Central Sector scheme of MNRE (2024): rooftop solar for one crore households by 2027; subsidy Rs 30,000-60,000 for 1-2 kW, Rs 60,000-78,000 for 2-3 kW and Rs 78,000 above 3 kW; collateral-free loans at about 7% up to 3 kW; a Model Solar Village in each district; trains over 3 lakh skilled workers.
Eligibility: a household that has not taken any other rooftop-solar subsidy; Central Financial Assistance depends on average monthly electricity use and the suitable rooftop capacity.
The Annual Survey of India's City Systems (ASICS) is conducted by which one of the following? Janaagraha Foundation.
Its 2023 report suggests India may be far more urban than the Census indicates.
The Eastern Nagaland Peoples' Organisation (ENPO), a party to the FNTA agreement, represents how many recognised Naga tribes of six eastern districts? Eight.
They are the Konyak, Sangtam, Chang, Khiamniungan, Yimkhiung, Tikhir, Phom and Sumi.

With reference to India-France cooperation, consider the following: 1. The TRISHNA satellite is a joint project of ISRO and CNES. 2. UPI has been launched in France. 3. France supports India's permanent seat in the UN Security Council. 4. France has no role in the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor. How many of the above of the above statements are correct? Only three.
France is a key stakeholder in IMEC.
Which one of the following is described as being developed by India in Seychelles to boost maritime surveillance? Assumption Island.
Seychelles is a pillar of SAGAR and Vision MAHASAGAR and lies near the Mozambique Channel. India also deployed a Coastal Surveillance Radar System there.
ALARA says radiation exposure should be kept as low as reasonably achievable, and its removal risks higher worker exposure.
See also the radiation safety notes in this month's set.
Reports indicated signs of genocide in the siege of El-Fasher by a paramilitary group.
The Darfur region lies in the west of Sudan.
The Masalit, Zaghawa and Fur communities were among those affected.
Kordofan, with El Obeid as its capital, and the Blue Nile state are other regions affected.
The text also notes that the smiling curve shows higher value in upstream activities like R&D and design and downstream activities like branding, while assembly in the middle earns less.
See also the manufacturing notes in this month's set.
The MSME Champion Scheme has which one of the following sets of components? Sustainable (ZED), Competitive (LEAN), Innovative.
The innovative component covers incubation, design and IPR.
The export obligation period for textile garments, footwear and leather products made with duty-free imported inputs was extended from 6 months to which one of the following? 12 months.
The extension gives greater flexibility to exporters.
Which one of the following committees recommended expanding the Negotiable Warehouse Receipt system and computerising storage management? Shanta Kumar Committee.
The Committee of 2014 also suggested converting FCI's conventional storage into silos with private participation. The CAG audit of 2023 urged phasing out CAP (Covered and Plinth) storage.
The Namo Bharat Regional Rapid Transit System (RRTS): it is a semi-high-speed commuter system of up to 180 km per hour.
The implementing agency is the National Capital Region Transport Corporation.

It differs from a metro in serving longer distances with fewer stops at higher speed, and from conventional trains in giving high-frequency point-to-point regional travel. The Delhi-Meerut RRTS cuts travel time from 3 hours to 60 minutes.
The NHAI has announced them along the National Highways.
BeeCorridors: they are continuous stretches of bee-friendly vegetation providing nectar and pollen round the year.
Only female bees have stingers, which are modified ovipositors. About a third of the world's food production depends on bees.
The 4P approach proposed to tackle dowry consists of which one of the following sets? Punishment, Protection, Prevention, Promotion.
It treats dowry as a socio-economic institution rooted in patriarchy and marriage markets and not merely a legal problem.
In the M.A.N.A.V. framework, which one of the following is represented by the letter 'M'? Moral and Ethical system.
It emphasises fairness, transparency and human oversight as non-negotiable principles in AI design.
The 'Thucydides trap' suggests a high risk of war in which one of the following situations? A rising power challenging a ruling power.
It is cited to explain rivalry between a rising China and the established US.
According to the UNHCR, how many people were forcibly displaced worldwide by the end of June 2025? More than 117 million.
They were displaced by persecution, conflict, violence or human rights violations. The Global Peace Index 2025 says global peacefulness has deteriorated every year since 2014.
